title: APIRouter.include_router method should catch when its own object is passed
body:
### First Check

- [X] I already searched in Google "How to X in FastAPI" and didn't find any information.
- [X] I already read and followed all the tutorial in the docs and didn't find an answer.
- [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [Pydantic](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic).
- [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [Swagger UI](https://github.com/swagger-api/swagger-ui).
- [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [ReDoc](https://github.com/Redocly/redoc).

### Commit to Help

- [X] I commit to help with one of those options 👆

### Example Code

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter

router = APIRouter(prefix='/api')

router.include_router(router) # Locks program
```


### Description

Passing a router's own object into the `include_router` method results in FastAPI locking up, requiring the Python process to be terminated.

This should be resolved by checking `if router is self: ...` and then raising some error. This is preferred to the current implementation because currently type checkers will not raise any flags and may require some tedious debugging.

Windows, macOS
